page: Amazon Web Services r6gd.2xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by an 8-core AWS Graviton processor built on the ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 architecture. Operating at 2.5 GHz, this instance features 8 physical cores with a dedicated CPU allocation and no hyperthreading. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of memory, yielding a high resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled as a 474 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume, and the network interface provides a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps under the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

Performance benchmarks indicate average multi-core capabilities, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 12133.23 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 5344.0. Memory bandwidth is a notable strength, reaching 472.5 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 101.11 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. However, single-core processing is relatively weak, as shown by a Geekbench single-core score of 930.0 and poor single-threaded bzip3 decompression. Large-block memory write speeds are measured at 47.4 GB/sec, and LLM inference tasks show lower efficiency, generating 35.03 tokens per second on a small 135M model.

The r6gd.2xlarge offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads by leveraging custom ARM-based Graviton processors, which typically deliver a favorable performance-per-watt ratio compared to traditional x86 architectures. The inclusion of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage eliminates the need for external block storage for temporary data. This hardware profile is well-suited for memory-intensive applications, database operations (scoring 5295.54 on Passmark database tests), Redis caching (achieving 9.53 million SET operations per second), and static web serving.
